Great effort on getting into the Warrior One pose, but I'd like to help fine-tune your position to make it even more effective and safe. Let’s make a few adjustments together.

Firstly, let’s focus on your spine. Right now, it seems a bit rounded. We want to aim for a straight and elongated spine to ensure we are engaging our core and maintaining balance. Try to tuck your tailbone slightly and draw your belly button towards your spine. This will help in straightening your back. Think of lengthening your body from the top of your head all the way to your feet.

Moving on to your arms, I noticed they are not fully extended upwards. We want to reach actively through the fingertips like you're trying to touch the ceiling. This active reach will help you engage your shoulders and upper back correctly. Make sure your shoulders are relaxed and not creeping up towards your ears; keep them down and back.

Lastly, let's talk about your legs. Your knee should be directly over your ankle on your front leg. This is important to protect your knee joint from strain. If your knee is pushing past your toes, shift your weight back slightly and adjust your stance so that you are forming a 90-degree angle with your front knee.

Let’s try these adjustments. Remember, yoga is a practice where we grow gradually, so take your time to feel each alignment in your body. A pose will feel strongest and most stable when properly aligned. You’re doing a fantastic job by being aware of your body and making these improvements!
